item.title: index
item.description: Rest of Europe 1866–1919 Wiki A narrative-research knowledge base on continental European history from the Austro-Prussian War through the First World War and its immediate aftermath.

item.title: Anticlericalism and the Separation (Laïcité)
item.description: Anticlericalism and the Separation (Laïcité) Anticlericalism was the doctrine and the policy of the Third Republic that sought to reduce the influence of the Catholic Church in public life and to establish the separation of the spiritual and the temporal powers.

item.title: The Ausgleich (Compromise) of 1867
item.description: The Ausgleich of 1867 The Ausgleich (“compromise,” in Hungarian kiegyezés) of 1867 was the constitutional settlement by which the Austrian Empire was transformed into the Dual Monarchy of Austria-Hungary.

item.title: Russian Autocracy
item.description: Russian Autocracy The Russian autocracy — samoderzhavie (самодержавіе, “self-rule”) — is the political principle by which the Emperor of All the Russias held his power in his own person, owing it to no constitution, no parliament, and no elected body, but directly to God alone.

item.title: Bonapartism
item.description: Bonapartism Bonapartism is the political tradition of Napoleonic authority — a plebiscitary Caesarism that joins democracy to authoritarian rule, claiming to embody the sovereignty of the people through the will of a single man.

item.title: The Kulturkampf (1871–c. 1879)
item.description: The Kulturkampf The Kulturkampf (“culture struggle”) was the conflict between the government of otto-von-bismarck and the Catholic Church in Prussia and the new German Empire in the 1870s, fought over the limits of the state’s authority against the claims of Rome.

item.title: The Eastern Question
item.description: The Eastern Question The Eastern Question — die orientalische Frage — is the European problem of the decline of the Ottoman Empire and the disposition of its territories, above all in the Balkans: the great standing issue of European diplomacy from the eighteenth century down to the world war.
